title: Build A Virtual Showroom With Clo! Skill-Up Webinar
description:
In this Skill-up Webinar, our official CLO designer walks you through a full workflow on how to build a room in CLO, optimize garments with and without the Everywear plugin, render 360 images, and create a virtual showroom using CLO-SET.

Download the files so you can follow along here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1jALpe-2MxeDNFSlcvchZxVNBR_LmMTLI?usp=sharing

Get EveryWear: https://connect.clo-set.com/everywear

Get CLO-SET: https://style.clo-set.com/aboutus

This live session was on August 8th. Join our next webinar to participate and ask questions!

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction
0:50 Project overview
06:07 Optimizing the showroom
12:39 Exporting the room
15:37 Optimizing the garments
29:13 Importing all assets
49:42 Rendering the 360 degree images
59:40 Creating the Virtual Showroom in CLO-SET
1:08:39 Q&A

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord- 

--- 
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/itsclo3d 
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/clo-virtual-fashion-inc-/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/clo3d/

markdown_content: ## Introduction to Building a Virtual Showroom in CLO This section introduces the process of creating a virtual showroom using CLO software, focusing on project setup, file management, and initial considerations for performance optimization. Key terms include CLO, Everywhere plugin, virtual showroom, and project folder structure. Daniel, a 3D Design and Implementation Specialist at CLO, demonstrates building a virtual showroom in CLO using the Everywhere plugin. The project files, including avatars, garments, and renderings, are organized in folders for easy access. The initial large project file contains a full room constructed from CLO pattern pieces and garments but is very heavy and requires a powerful computer to run smoothly. --- ## Assessing Project Complexity and Performance Metrics in CLO This section covers how to evaluate the complexity of CLO projects using performance and mesh statistics, including triangle count, vertices, and frame rates, which are critical for optimizing heavy 3D scenes. To understand project heaviness, Daniel shows how to check statistics in CLO by navigating to **Settings > Display > Environment** and enabling **Show Frame Rate**, which displays real-time data on triangles (tris), vertices, patterns, trims, CPU cores, and frame rates in the 3D window. - Example stats for the full room project: - 3.4 million triangles - 750,000 vertices - 448 patterns - 15 trims - 12 CPU cores used Higher particle distances on garments increase quality but also add data load, contributing to heavier projects and slower rendering. The room is built at true-to-life scale, with walls approximately 3.5 meters tall and 600 thickness in rendering. --- ## Optimization Techniques for Virtual Showroom Rooms in CLO This section explains methods to optimize CLO projects by reducing polygon counts, switching mesh types, and exporting optimized room geometry as OBJ files for better performance. ### Reducing Polygon Count - The original heavy project with over 1.4 million triangles was optimized to around 63,000 triangles by: - Increasing particle distance on flat pattern pieces (e.g., walls) to values as high as 500, which reduces mesh density without quality loss on flat surfaces. - Adjusting particle distances carefully on curved objects (e.g., windows) to preserve shape quality, typically setting particle distance to 200 for rounded shapes. ### Changing Mesh Type from Triangles to Quads - Changing mesh settings from triangles to quads reduces face and vertex count significantly while maintaining visual quality, beneficial mainly for square or flat objects. - Quads are less effective on rounded shapes because they create edgy artifacts when particle distance is increased. - For example, walls set to quads drastically reduce face count from 600+ to under 200, improving performance. ### Exporting as OBJ to Further Optimize - Pattern pieces are converted to OBJ files to simplify the geometry and reduce computational load. - The ceiling is exported separately to keep navigation manageable. - Export settings: - Scale: millimeters - Thickness enabled for walls and ceiling to preserve volume - Texture files saved with absolute paths - Exported OBJs are easier to handle in CLO than pattern pieces with particle distance settings. --- ## Garment Optimization Using the Everywhere Plugin in CLO This section details how to reduce garment polygon counts using the Everywhere plugin, balancing quality and performance, and explains how to optimize garments for different avatar types. ### Optimizing Garments - The Everywhere plugin (version 2024.1.142 used) analyzes polygon counts for garments and avatars, allowing users to set a maximum triangle count. - Example: A garment with 381,000 triangles was optimized to below 100,000 triangles by automatically adjusting particle distances across all pattern pieces (e.g., from 5 to ~10). - The plugin can also pack UVs, create material lists, and prepare garments for game export, but the focus here is on polygon optimization. ### Auto Fitting Garments to Different Avatars - CLO provides an **Auto Fitting** feature (formerly Auto Grading) to fit garments onto different avatars without manual grading. - The process: - Delete the current avatar. - Load a new avatar (e.g., female or child mannequins from CLO Connect Marketplace). - Apply Auto Fitting to automatically drape and resize garments to the new avatar. - Limitations: - It's a quick fit, not perfect grading; minor issues like hem tangling may occur. - Best used for demonstration or fast prototyping. --- ## Managing Avatars and Garments in the Scene This section explains how to add and position multiple avatars and garments in CLO’s 3D workspace, including handling gizmos for movement and manual alignment. - When importing garments, use the **Add** option instead of **Open** to keep existing scene content. - The gizmo tool allows moving avatars and garments but only appears for the last added avatar; moving multiple avatars simultaneously is not supported. - Common workflow: - Add garments and avatars separately. - Manually position garments over avatars ensuring no clipping. - Use library poses (e.g., female V2 pose “attention 03”) to adjust avatar poses. - Use **Show Avatar Joints** (Shift + X) to adjust limb positions for better fit. - Save the project frequently after positioning to prevent data loss. --- ## Importing and Combining Room and Garment Assets This section covers combining the optimized room OBJ files with garment projects and additional garment assets, preparing a complete virtual showroom scene. - Load the optimized room OBJ files (project and ceiling) into a CLO project using **Add** mode. - Import optimized garment projects (male, female, kid) and position manually as described. - Additional garments and props (e.g., sunglasses, shoes, folded garments, plants) can be imported as separate projects. - Use the **Freeze** and **Strengthen** functions in CLO to lock certain items in place, and **Show/Hide Colors** to reduce visual clutter. - Note: Exporting/importing OBJ files resets material settings, so materials such as metals and lights need to be reassigned manually. --- ## Rendering Setup and Best Practices for Virtual Showrooms in CLO This section explains how to configure rendering settings, camera setup for 360° panorama images, and preparation for uploading virtual showroom content to CLOset. ### Rendering Settings - Image size: 16:9 format with max resolution 8000 x 4096 pixels; file size below 100 MB recommended. - Rendering output format: PNG with transparency enabled. - Light and render properties have preset files for quick setup, including GPU usage for Windows (unsupported on some Macs). - Noise threshold adjusted to 0.010 or lower (e.g., 0.005) for less grainy renders. ### Camera and Panorama Rendering - Change camera lens type from **Default** to **Panorama** to capture 360° images. - Adjust render position within the room to simulate a "standing spot." - Interactive rendering allows previewing the panoramic effect with a grid overlay for positioning. - Multiple panorama shots from different angles provide navigation points in the virtual showroom. --- ## Creating Virtual Showrooms in CLOset This section describes how to use CLOset to create an interactive virtual showroom experience by uploading assets, adding navigation points, and linking 3D content. ### CLOset Workroom and Assortment Room Setup - Upload all garment and project files into a CLOset workroom. - Create an assortment room (e.g., "Virtual Showroom Demo") to collect all media assets. - Import panorama renderings into the assortment room. ### Navigation Points and Content Linking - Add navigation points with custom arrows that link different 360° panorama images, allowing users to navigate within the virtual showroom. - Navigation arrows can be customized in color, opacity, and position on the floor. - Additional 3D or 2D content (e.g., swimwear outfits) can be added as interactive points linking to CLO 3D viewers. - The virtual showroom becomes an interactive space where users can move between viewpoints and inspect garments and accessories. --- ## Frequently Asked Questions and Additional Tips This section provides insights into development time, external software integration, marketplace imports, and future prospects for virtual showrooms. - Building and populating the virtual showroom took approximately one to two weeks, including design, texture sourcing, and garment placement. - Users can import 3D assets from external marketplaces (e.g., wheelchairs, cars) as OBJ or FBX files for use within CLO. - Image quality can be enhanced using AI tools like Clear.ai or rendering in external software such as Unreal Engine or Blender. - CLO does not currently support direct use of Apple VR glasses for virtual showrooms, but interest in VR integration exists. - The **Gizmo** tool cannot select and move avatars and garments simultaneously; this is a known limitation and feature request. - Free virtual showrooms require a CLOset account, with some limitations based on account type. Pricing details are available at clo-set.com. - Additional resources include CLO’s YouTube tutorials on virtual showrooms and the Everywhere plugin for garment optimization and rigging. --- ## Summary This guide covers the end-to-end process of building a virtual showroom in CLO, from project assessment and optimization through garment fitting, room assembly, rendering, and final deployment in CLOset. It emphasizes balancing performance and quality using mesh optimization, OBJ exports, and the Everywhere plugin, and demonstrates how to create interactive virtual environments with 360° panorama images and navigation points. The workflow allows users to showcase fashion collections in immersive virtual spaces with manageable computational demands.

Quads are less effective on rounded shapes because they create edgy artifacts when particle distance is increased. - For example, walls set to quads drastically reduce face count from 600+ to under 200, improving performance. ### Exporting as OBJ to Further Optimize - Pattern pieces are converted to OBJ files to simplify the geometry and reduce computational load. - The ceiling is exported separately to keep navigation manageable. - Export settings: - Scale: millimeters - Thickness enabled for walls and ceiling to preserve volume - Texture files saved with absolute paths - Exported OBJs are easier to handle in CLO than pattern pieces with particle distance settings. --- ## Garment Optimization Using the Everywhere Plugin in CLO This section details how to reduce garment polygon counts using the Everywhere plugin, balancing quality and performance, and explains how to optimize garments for different avatar types. ### Optimizing Garments - The Everywhere plugin (version 2024.1.142 used) analyzes polygon counts for garments and avatars, allowing users to set a maximum triangle count. - Example: A garment with 381,000 triangles was optimized to below 100,000 triangles by automatically adjusting particle distances across all pattern pieces (e.g., from 5 to ~10). - The plugin can also pack UVs, create material lists, and prepare garments for game export, but the focus here is on polygon optimization. ### Auto Fitting Garments to Different Avatars - CLO provides an **Auto Fitting** feature (formerly Auto Grading) to fit garments onto different avatars without manual grading. - The process: - Delete the current avatar. - Load a new avatar (e.g., female or child mannequins from CLO Connect Marketplace). - Apply Auto Fitting to automatically drape and resize garments to the new avatar. - Limitations: - It's a quick fit, not perfect grading; minor issues like hem tangling may occur. - Best used for demonstration or fast prototyping. --- ## Managing Avatars and Garments in the Scene This section explains how to add and position multiple avatars and garments in CLO’s 3D workspace, including handling gizmos for movement and manual alignment. - When importing garments, use the **Add** option instead of **Open** to keep existing scene content. - The gizmo tool allows moving avatars and garments but only appears for the last added avatar; moving multiple avatars simultaneously is not supported. - Common workflow: - Add garments and avatars separately. - Manually position garments over avatars ensuring no clipping. - Use library poses (e.g., female V2 pose “attention 03”) to adjust avatar poses. - Use **Show Avatar Joints** (Shift + X) to adjust limb positions for better fit. - Save the project frequently after positioning to prevent data loss.

chunks.content: - The gizmo tool allows moving avatars and garments but only appears for the last added avatar; moving multiple avatars simultaneously is not supported. - Common workflow: - Add garments and avatars separately. - Manually position garments over avatars ensuring no clipping. - Use library poses (e.g., female V2 pose “attention 03”) to adjust avatar poses. - Use **Show Avatar Joints** (Shift + X) to adjust limb positions for better fit. - Save the project frequently after positioning to prevent data loss. --- ## Importing and Combining Room and Garment Assets This section covers combining the optimized room OBJ files with garment projects and additional garment assets, preparing a complete virtual showroom scene. - Load the optimized room OBJ files (project and ceiling) into a CLO project using **Add** mode. - Import optimized garment projects (male, female, kid) and position manually as described. - Additional garments and props (e.g., sunglasses, shoes, folded garments, plants) can be imported as separate projects. - Use the **Freeze** and **Strengthen** functions in CLO to lock certain items in place, and **Show/Hide Colors** to reduce visual clutter. - Note: Exporting/importing OBJ files resets material settings, so materials such as metals and lights need to be reassigned manually. --- ## Rendering Setup and Best Practices for Virtual Showrooms in CLO This section explains how to configure rendering settings, camera setup for 360° panorama images, and preparation for uploading virtual showroom content to CLOset. ### Rendering Settings - Image size: 16:9 format with max resolution 8000 x 4096 pixels; file size below 100 MB recommended. - Rendering output format: PNG with transparency enabled. - Light and render properties have preset files for quick setup, including GPU usage for Windows (unsupported on some Macs). - Noise threshold adjusted to 0.010 or lower (e.g., 0.005) for less grainy renders. ### Camera and Panorama Rendering - Change camera lens type from **Default** to **Panorama** to capture 360° images. - Adjust render position within the room to simulate a "standing spot." - Interactive rendering allows previewing the panoramic effect with a grid overlay for positioning. - Multiple panorama shots from different angles provide navigation points in the virtual showroom. --- ## Creating Virtual Showrooms in CLOset This section describes how to use CLOset to create an interactive virtual showroom experience by uploading assets, adding navigation points, and linking 3D content. ### CLOset Workroom and Assortment Room Setup - Upload all garment and project files into a CLOset workroom. - Create an assortment room (e.g., "Virtual Showroom Demo") to collect all media assets. - Import panorama renderings into the assortment room. ### Navigation Points and Content Linking - Add navigation points with custom arrows that link different 360° panorama images, allowing users to navigate within the virtual showroom. - Navigation arrows can be customized in color, opacity, and position on the floor. - Additional 3D or 2D content (e.g., swimwear outfits) can be added as interactive points linking to CLO 3D viewers.
